description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of child nodes (tree width) and the accuracy percentage (Accuracy@1) for two different language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, in the context of Visual Navigation and geometry problems. The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)," is linear and ranges from 1 to 7, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy@111 and and and 1-1, and the to 7, is also linear, ranging from 15% to 35%, with tick labels at every 5% interval. The plot features two lines: the solid blue line represents GPT-4o, and the dashed blue line with 'x' markers represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet. GPT-4o starts at 24.4% accuracy at a tree width of 1, increases to 28.9% at a width of 3, peaks at 34.4% at a width of 5, and then decreases to 31.1% at a width of 7. Claude-3.5-Sonnet starts at 26.7% accuracy at a tree width of 1, increases to 27.8% at a width of 3, decreases to 24.4% at a width of 5, and then further decreases to 20.0% at a width of 7. The plot shows that Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforms GPT-4o across all tree widths, with a notable peak for GPT-4o at a tree width of 5.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
